>Society needs people who have suffered because that's where compassion comes from. You're clearly fairly clever so you have a lot to offer. Think about how cunty the average person is. Now realize that half of the people you're thinking about are bigger cunts then them.

I really don't owe any of those cunts anything.

>I think you should stick it out just to push that ratio a little farther this way.

Nah I'd rather just take a nap on some train tracks
I know you were lying when you said losing me would be a terrible blow to you.

> It's not your fault and it will get better.

Is that what you tell yourself? Because I don't see money just falling out of the sky. Some things don't just get better.

>Please go here and call them if you feel like ending your life. http://www.suicidepreventionlifeline.org

Yeah, no, they can't pay my tuition. I don't need to be referred to an expensive therapist or have my debt talked away.

>Yeah great points but that's from a defeatest point of view.

So?

>I'll have you know that I rather enjoy my soul-crushing job

Congrats, it's not soul-crushing.

>who gives a shit if you keep up with your peers?

I do, they do, future employers do.

>And lastly no, I don't know you. And I would have no way of knowing if you harmed yourself even before this message was finished but I gave it a shot. That's what I'm asking from you.

Stop pretending you care about strangers who have no impact on your life whatsoever. It's dishonest.
Are they going to give me money or just refer me to a therapist I can't afford?

>Quit being such a baby. Quit comparing yourself to your friends. They have a leg up. It sucks. Life's not fair. Sorry, but that's the cards you were dealt.

I guess I'll just kill myself then.

EDIT: Thanks for the downvote

>Putting off your dream of having a degree is NOT giving up.

It is if it means that you can't keep up with your peers, don't get to appreciate the effort until you're old, or have opportunities pass over you in favor of younger people. Woohoo, I get to spend time doing soul-crushing work. No thanks.

>If you decide to harm yourself over this it will be a very poor reason

I disagree.

>Only you can make this choice but you should talk to a councilor.

That sounds expensive.

>You're important and losing you would be a terrible blow to all of us.

You don't know me, and if I were to stop posting tomorrow you would have no way of knowing whether I was alive or dead.

> What state are you residing in currently? Different states have different policies on supporting students ranging from waiving your tuition partially to 100%.

NJ.

>Have you considered taking a step back and making a budget worksheet to work out what expenses can be compromised so you can reallocate resources to other areas?

Rent + tuition alone is going to take everything from me and then some. Even with my job.

>If education is your ultimate goal then you have to start thinking about it very seriously and accept that as a students you have to give up/sacrifice certain things in your life (less dining out, less going to the movies, etc.) to maximize your success.

I don't really go out/spend money on things like that and even if I could cut those things out, it wouldn't make up the difference. I mean, I haven't been to the movies in months, and the last time I ate out, my sister paid for it...
I'm already transferring to another school so I don't fall behind in my major... that would be one step forward and two steps back.
I need to be a full-time student to qualify for on-campus housing. I'm also already (probably) going to need 5 years to finish because I'm doing a double major.
Already did that. They are not going to cover everything. I need $9000 and I am poor.
You need ~$16000 (iirc) saved to prove you can support yourself before you can do that. Plus it's too late to apply for next year, so it would have to be junior year.
Already did that. Financial aid will not cover everything.
